The image shows a single mango leaf that is completely brown, desiccated, and shriveled. The leaf is dry, dead-looking, and curled, with no green tissue remaining. This pattern of necrosis and dieback is not consistent with powdery mildew (white powder), sooty mould (black sooty coating), or anthracnose (dark spots/lesions with irregular margins). Instead, the complete browning, wilting, and drying of the shoot tip/leaf is characteristic of Die Back, where the tissue dies from the tip backward.
